turns.content: My closest friend has cancelled plans with me twice this month.

I'm sorry to hear that. It can be really disappointing when plans fall through, especially with someone close to you. Have you had a chance to talk to your friend about it? Sometimes there might be reasons behind their cancellations that you’re not aware of.
Both times they said they were exhausted from work. We haven't really talked much otherwise.

That makes sense; work can be really draining. It might be worth reaching out to check in on them. You could express that you understand they’re busy but that you miss spending time together. It could open up a conversation and help you both reconnect. How do you feel about reaching out?
I don't know whether they're losing interest in the friendship or genuinely overwhelmed.

It’s understandable to feel uncertain in this situation. It might help to approach the conversation with an open mind. You could ask how they’ve been feeling and if there’s anything you can do to support them. This way, you can gauge their interest in the friendship without putting too much pressure on them. It’s possible they’re just going through a tough time and still value your friendship. How do you think they might respond?
Would it be reasonable for me to stop initiating plans for a week or two and see whether they reach out?

That sounds like a reasonable approach. Giving them some space might help you see if they reach out on their own. It can also give you a chance to reflect on how you feel about the friendship. Just remember to take care of yourself during that time, too. If they don’t reach out, you can always decide how you want to proceed from there. How do you feel about taking that step?
